claim: PJM's public record for Message 105558 changed materially. A 17:57:41 EPT snapshot identified TLR Level 5a commencing at 18:00 for flowgate 27750; the 20:47:46 EPT snapshot identifies TLR Level 1 commencing at 21:00 under the same message ID. This supports a public-record correction or supersession and a lower prospective TLR level, but does not establish when Level 5a ended, whether transactions were curtailed or reallocated during the interval, or whether every downstream recipient received the updated state.

falsifier: An authoritative PJM version history showing that the two displays refer to different operational records despite the shared message ID, or that the earlier Level 5a snapshot was a display artifact that never represented an issued state, would alter or falsify the correction/supersession interpretation.
firstUnsupportedArrow: PJM current-page correction or supersession -> all transaction operators and downstream data recipients received the update -> earlier curtailment instructions ceased or were reversed -> affected consequences were repaired
omissions: No explicit cancellation, release, correction notice, or public version history for Message 105558 was retrieved.
The exact time at which the public record changed from Level 5a to Level 1 is unknown between the two snapshots.
No interchange tags, curtailment identities, megawatts, acknowledgments, or completed TLR log were retrieved.
No evidence establishes whether Level 5a instructions were acted upon before the 21:00 Level 1 state.
No evidence establishes propagation to OASIS records, NERC logs, transaction operators, downstream datasets, search indexes, or AI summaries.
The current page does not prove consequence repair or complete extinction of any earlier operational effect.

failures.detail: The live PJM page overwrites Message 105558 state without exposing the prior version or an explicit correction chain.
No public completed TLR log or recipient acknowledgment chain was retrieved.

rivalHypotheses: PJM deliberately downgraded the constraint after Level 5a relief or changing grid conditions.
The earlier Level 5a entry was corrected because it was erroneous or premature rather than operationally completed.
Reuse of the same message ID is the normal lifecycle mechanism for TLR updates, but the public interface still does not expose custody and propagation history.
